text:
sarah_support: Hey team — customer reports Console actions greyed out and API calls returning 403 when switching into their Project 'orbit'. They accepted the Okta invite yesterday and can see the project in the UI but 'Create deployment' buttons are disabled. Can someone triage? :thinking_face:

jordan_engineer: Do we have a repro curl or error trace? Also confirm auth method (SSO/API key).

sarah_support: SSO via Okta + SCIM group mappings. Quick repro steps from customer:
1) Sign in through Okta -> console loads
2) Switch org -> select project `orbit`
3) Click "New deployment" -> button greys out + toast "permission denied"

matt_sre: Can you run a curl against the REST endpoint with the user's token so we can see the API response? `Authorization: Bearer <user_jwt>` ideally sanitized.

sarah_support: Pasting sanitized output we got from the customer support logs:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ...REDACTED..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/orbit/deployments
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"user lacks project:deploy permission"}
```

jordan_engineer: That indicates the user's token doesn't have the expected project role claim. Can you decode the token (sanitized) to inspect claims? Look for `roles` or `groups` claims and any `project:` prefixes.

sarah_support: Decoded token (sanitized): `groups: ["okta:devs"]`, `roles: []`. They reported they were moved between org labels last week (org rename / merge).

matt_sre: Known edge case: our SCIM normalizer can drop `project:` role claims when a SCIM group rename collides in the org-merge path. Workaround is to trigger a SCIM resync or re-invite the user, then force a session refresh.

idp_sync_bot: @sarah_support Resync job queued (id rsync-20240408-179). Estimated 2m.

sarah_support: Resync finished but customer still got 403. They logged out/in and retried — still 403 in the same browser tab.

jordan_engineer: If the token in the tab is cached we need the user to re-auth (logout/login) or clear session cookies. Also check backend authz cache for stale membership mapping (we keep a TTL + explicit invalidation on some events).

sarah_support: Customer did a hard refresh + logout/login. New token now contains `roles: ["project:orbit:editor"]` but when they retried previously-open tab it still showed disabled UI. After clearing the tab/session it worked.

matt_sre: Root cause looks like a combination of SCIM group rename + authz cache not invalidating for that principal. Sequence: SCIM rename created duplicate group identifiers, resync fixed membership in identity store but our RBAC cache kept old mapping until session/token refresh.

jordan_engineer: I'll file an internal bug and a follow-up patch. Short term: docs/update support runbook to recommend: 1) trigger SCIM resync, 2) force user logout/login, 3) advise clearing browser state if UI still shows disabled actions.

sarah_support: Customer confirmed access restored after logout/login + hard refresh. I'll mark the ticket "resolved (workaround applied)" and link the internal bug for a permanent fix. :white_check_mark:

matt_sre: Creating BUG-5639: after SCIM resync trigger authz cache invalidation for affected principals. Also adding a note to the support KB about this replay scenario.

jordan_engineer: Thanks team. Also add a small diagnostic snippet to the KB for support engineers:
```
# quick diagnostic
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/<proj>/deployments -i
# check token claims (sanitized) for `roles` and `groups`
```

sarah_support: QA will confirm the bugfix next week, closing this support thread for now.
